title: Choosing between Django and FastAPI: what each one assumes

videos.script: You can already write Python. This course is about putting it behind a web address, where strangers send it requests and expect an answer in milliseconds. {{request}} Python has two frameworks that most teams reach for. Django, which arrives with almost everything a website needs. And FastAPI, which arrives with very little, and asks you to choose the rest. {{two}} They are not rivals in the way people argue about online. Each one assumes something about the application you are building. Django assumes pages, a database and people logging in. FastAPI assumes JSON, type hints and a lot of waiting. Where the assumptions hold, the work is fast. Where they do not, you fight the framework. {{assume}} So today you make each of them do the same small thing. One endpoint, written twice. Then you read the two answers line by line. {{compare}} Django sends four security headers you never asked for. FastAPI publishes a description of your API you never wrote. Those two details tell you more about each framework than any comparison chart. {{headers}} Before that, you check your machine. It is the one the python course built, and from lesson 4 on it grows a database, a queue and a web server. {{lab}} By the end of the lesson you can say which framework fits a project, and why.
